Why is it bad?

https://bugcrowd.com/try-bugcrowd
Most widely-publicized exploits have one or 
two dangerous attributes. 
Log4Shell has ﬁve.

https://bugcrowd.com/try-bugcrowd
Useful Remote Code Execution is very ﬂexible This exploit is useful for a huge variety of 
criminal goals
Easy CVE-2021-44228 is simple to exploit
Unsophisticated attacks are already 
underway providing “cover ﬁre” for stealthier 
adversaries
Persistent Log4j is often deeply embedded in 
applications
More dependancies means more testing 
before a patch can be applied safely
Common The Log4j library is everywhere, and often 
hard to ﬁnd
If something is diﬃcult to ﬁnd it becomes 
diﬃcult to ﬁx
Flexible Log4j accepts input from a very wide 
variety of sources
The vulnerability can be triggered in a huge 
variety of ways

https://bugcrowd.com/try-bugcrowd
What happens next?

https://bugcrowd.com/try-bugcrowd
So far…
•Benevolent bug bounty hunting and vulnerability research
•Malicious exploitation from weakly motivated attackers
•First-stage WAF evasion R&D
•Non-HTTP exploitation vector R&D (SMTP , DNS, RMI, malicious 
access points, etc)
•Opportunistic crypto-miners and botnet herders (Kinseng, 
Hushing, Mirai)
•Ransomware groups and IABs manually investigating internal 
networks

https://bugcrowd.com/try-bugcrowd
What’s next
•Increased patching and blocking will cause casual bug hunters 
and weakly motivated attackers to lose interest
•Second-stage payload reliability R&D will continue, likely funded 
by cybercriminal groups
•Ransomware and RaaS malware deployment will commence
•Potential self-propagating worm with malware payload (a la 
Wannacry)

https://bugcrowd.com/try-bugcrowd
Defender priorities
1.Activate WAF to cut out noise
2.Update asset registry of known instances of Log4J
3.Patch or disable Log4j where possible
4.Apply workarounds if patching isn’t possible
5.Implement egress network and DNS ﬁltering
6.Ask SOC to treat attacks against known Log4j as incidents

https://bugcrowd.com/try-bugcrowd
